title: STM32MP257FAK3 - Marvell 88E1512 IC probe error
content:
Hi,

I'm bringing up Ethernet (RGMII) on a custom STM32MP257 board using a Marvell 88E1512 PHY.

The MAC driver loads successfully, the PHY is detected, but bringing the interface up fails with a timeout.
I have attached the driver code, dts and pinctrl.dtsi for you reference.

pins1 {

pinmux = <STM32_PINMUX('A', 9, AF10)>; /* ETH1_MDC */

bias-disable;

drive-push-pull;

slew-rate = <2>;

st,io-clk-edge = <0>;

st,io-retime = <0>;

st,io-delay-path = <0>;

st,io-delay = <0>;

};

scraped_replies.html:
From the logs, the PHY is initially detected, but later all PHY registers read 0xFFFF and phy_poll_reset failed (-110) indicates the PHY is no longer responding over MDIO.

A few things I'd verify first:

  • Double-check the PHY reset timing against the 88E1512 datasheet (hold/reset delays after power-up).
  • Confirm the RGMII clock mode (internal PHY delay vs. MAC delay) and DTS phy-mode match your hardware.
  • Verify MDIO/MDC signal integrity during the failure (not just reset/clock) and ensure the PHY power rails remain stable.
  • Compare your DTS and pinctrl with the STM32MP257 Ethernet reference design to rule out pinmux or clock configuration issues.

Since the PHY ID changes to 0xFFFF, this looks more like a hardware, reset, or MDIO communication issue than a MAC driver problem.

Hi,

I verified the hardware signals using an oscilloscope:

  • The PHY reset sequence is correct and follows the timing requirements.

  • MDC and MDIO signals are present and look normal.

  • The reference clocks are also present and stable.

  • The PHY power rails remain stable during boot.

I also noticed that the Marvell driver (marvell.c) is successfully matched with the PHY and m88e1510_config_init() is called. The kernel detects the PHY with ID 0x01410dd0, but once the configuration starts, subsequent MDIO reads return 0xFFFF, and phy_poll_reset() times out with -110.

My PHY device is Marvell 88E1512, while the driver appears to use the 88E1510 configuration path.
Is there any additional patch or specific support required for the 88E1512 on the STM32MP257 platform? Is there a recommended driver update or patch that should be applied?

Any guidance would be appreciated.
